title: Carrier screening before pregnancy
what: This test shows whether a person carries a hidden gene change that does not harm them but can be passed to a child. Usually both future parents take it.
why: When planning a pregnancy, if genetic conditions run in the family, if the partners are related, and with IVF.
duration: the blood draw usually takes 5 minutes; results usually come in 2 to 4 weeks
tell_doctor: If genetic conditions, or children with them, have been in either family
If you and your partner are related
If you are already pregnant, and how far along
If you had a blood transfusion or a bone marrow transplant

prepare.title: Counseling
prepare.text: It is best to talk with a geneticist ahead of time about which conditions the test covers.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You usually do not need to fast. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: Your partner
prepare.text: Agree on who goes first, or do it together. That gets the couple an answer faster.

bring: Information about conditions in both families
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
Blood is taken from a vein. Sometimes saliva is collected instead
The samples are sent to a genetics lab
feel: A quick prick, like a normal blood test
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse, and they will help you lie down
after: Results usually come in 2 to 4 weeks
Almost everyone carries some gene changes. This is normal
There is a risk for the child when both partners carry a change in the same gene
If that happens, a geneticist will explain your options

faq.q: If I am a carrier, am I sick?
faq.a: No. A carrier is usually healthy. The change matters only for future children.

faq.q: Is it enough if only one partner is tested?
faq.a: Sometimes testing starts with one. But an accurate answer about the child's risk needs both results.

reminders.text: Genetic test before pregnancy tomorrow. Bring ID for both partners.
